A way to suggest places where visiting one spot requires prior knowledge from others is provided by Exploration Space Theory (EST): it models “prerequisite dependencies” among points of interest as a prerequisite-aware structure, and recommends the next “valid” location based on the user’s allowable exploration states (order ideals) rather than treating all POIs as independent [1]. The Exploration Space Recommender System (ESRS) then produces fringe-guided recommendations that come with a structural validity certificate and explains why each recommendation is a sound next step [1].

If you instead want route-style discovery with interactive information about places along the way, WalkRAG recommends walkable urban itineraries while retrieving information conversationally as you move through POIs under spatial constraints [3]. If your focus is geospatially consistent recommendation rather than prerequisites, SPAR builds and preserves urban spatial knowledge in the recommendation process using geospatial embeddings and geospatial pretraining [2].
